words: oh hey Berry. the bit that keeps coming back is the school underwater, and me swimming down the corridor instead of walking. the light was all wobbly like looking through a dirty fish tank.
yeah exactly. I couldn't even hear anything except sort of a muffled hum. and I could breathe fine, which didn't feel weird in the dream at all.
I went into my old classroom from primary school. the desks were all covered in seaweed and the other pupils were little silver fish sitting at them, like they were in my class.
I don't think I even looked for a seat, I just sort of hovered there in the doorway. my old teacher Mr Hale was at the front writing on the board. he still had his brown jacket on.
no, he didn't turn round. he just kept writing, and then slowly he turned into this huge orange octopus. still had one arm up holding the chalk, like he hadn't stopped being the teacher.
it didn't scare me, more like just something that happens. I stayed in the doorway watching him. there was no sound of the chalk, just the water moving a bit.

not sure, not long I think. then the school bell rang but it came out as a big stream of bubbles going up to the surface, and all the fish swam out of the window at once. just zoomed out in a silver rush.
I tried to follow them, and then I woke up. that's all I remember.
probably the moment the bell went and the bubbles streamed up, with all the fish turning toward the window at once. that felt like the whole dream in one second.
yeah I think he was still there by the board, but I wasn't looking at him by then, my eyes were on the fish and the bubbles. I don't know if he stopped writing or not.
maybe it got a bit cooler, like a current came in when they all moved. but the wobbly murky light stayed the same, all blue and green.
I don't remember feeling glad, no. it was all just ordinary to me, even the octopus. the silver fish leaving was more interesting than anything else.

the first thing I remember is the light, those wobbly beams coming down from above, and then I knew I was at my primary school but the whole school was underwater. I was already breathing fine, and I just swam down the corridor.
yeah, that's it. you got it all. the only thing is I'm not entirely sure if the water got cooler or if I just felt a current from them moving, but close enough.
yes, I would. that'd be good.
the closest for me would be the messy, wobbly underwater light in murky blue and green, like looking through dirty glass. that's the part I'd want right.
just imagine me how it seems. I don't have a clear picture of myself in it anyway.

the light looks right to me, all murky blue and green with the wobbly beams. mr hale as the octopus is good too, still holding the chalk in one arm like he was mid-write. the fish at the desks are just how I remember them, little silver ones facing the front.
the first one looks right — the wobbly light coming down from above and me swimming along. it's exactly that murky blue-green.
the second one is right too, the classroom with the desks covered in seaweed and the little silver fish at them. it looks ordinary, not dramatic, which is how it felt.
yeah, that looks right. mr hale still has his brown jacket on and he's mid-turn, like it's just happening slowly. the doorway view with all the fish facing the front is there too.

it looks right, the bubbles streaming up and the fish all starting to go. but in my dream it was more like a big single stream of bubbles from the bell, not separate little bubbles. and the water felt like it moved, but the drawing's close.
that's good, a big stream of bubbles would be better. when they moved it was a bit cooler round me, like a current, but I don't know if that shows.
okay, I'll wait for the rest and tell you if any of it looks off. the stream of bubbles being one big column from the bell is the main thing to fix.
the third one is now the one with the bell going and the bubble stream? or is that a new picture after the doorway? I'm just checking.
yeah, the newer one is right. I'm at the window trying to follow them, and the fish are already out. the water outside looks the same murky blue-green, not clear.
